This is Mbira Dance. ancient.
on_screen: Title card: Mbira Dance · Zimbabwe · ancient

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Mbira Dance originates from the Shona people of Zimbabwe and is linked to ancient spiritual practices involving communication with ancestral spirits.
Archaeological evidence dates the mbira instrument back to the twelfth century, indicating the long-standing tradition of this dance.
It is passed down through generations, primarily performed by tribal elders during religious ceremonies.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: The dance is performed during religious rituals to lure spirits through spirit mediums, facilitating communication with ancestors.
It is a powerful spiritual practice within the Shona community, reflecting their beliefs about the spirit world and fertility.
The dance is not for entertainment but for communal spiritual expression.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The dance is accompanied by the mbira, a plucked lamellophone producing melodic patterns, supported by drums (ngomas) and hosho shakers.
The music is polyrhythmic, with interlocking patterns creating complex rhythms.
Listen for the mbira, ngoma drums, hosho shakers.
The pulse is polyrhythmic, layered interlocking patterns.
The mbira produces bright, melodic plucked tones layered over steady drum beats and rattling hosho shakers, creating a textured, polyrhythmic soundscape that supports trance and spirit invocation.

scenes.title: The people
narration: The dance is traditionally performed by elders of the Shona tribes who serve as custodians of the spiritual and cultural knowledge embedded in the Mbira Dance.
Mbira Dance is specific to the Shona people of Zimbabwe.
Mbira Dance is part of the ritualistic category of Zimbabwean dances, alongside other spiritual dances like Dinhe and Mhande.

scenes.title: Family tree
narration: Mbira Dance is sibling of Jerusarema: Another Shona dance with polyrhythmic drumming but more acrobatic and performed at social events.
Mbira Dance is sibling of Dinhe: Religious dance also used to lure spirits, featuring war and joy movements.
Mbira Dance is sibling of Mhande: Midlands tribal dance with spiritual importance, sharing ritualistic context.

scenes.title: A respectful note
narration: Mbira Dance is a sacred ritual performed to communicate with ancestral spirits and should not be performed outside its spiritual context or by outsiders without permission.
